The tiddler stays one tiddler; no helper tiddlers are created. ## Features - **Toggle per tiddler** - an *outline* button in the view toolbar. Off means the normal view. - **Same rendering** - the tiddler renders exactly as usual; outline mode only adds data attributes, a selection frame and key handling. - **Units** - list items, lists, headings (with sections), paragraphs, code blocks, tables, opened HTML containers, transclusion lines, and widgets or macro calls (one opaque unit each). - **Type badges** - a small, faint label next to every unit shows what it is (paragraph, h2, code-block, bullet, ...), also on the editor field; they take no space. Settings: all (default), headings only, off. - **Selection** - click, Up/Down, Left/Right to the parent / first child, Escape clears. - **Move** - Alt-Up/Alt-Down swap a unit with its sibling, subtree included. Moves stay inside the parent. - **Indent** - Tab/Shift-Tab demote/promote list items and headings with their subtrees. - **In-place editor** - Enter or a double-click opens TW's own edit widget at the unit: a compact one-line field by default, optionally the full editor with toolbar. Lists and headings are edited without their marker; nesting stays with Tab/Shift-Tab. Ctrl-Enter saves, Enter saves and starts a new unit, Escape discards, Ctrl-Up/Down save and move the editor to the previous/next unit. - **Delete** - the Delete key removes the selection with everything below it, after a small yes/no menu (a heading: with its section or just the heading); list items without sub-items go at once (a setting). - **Split and merge** - Enter in the middle of a list item splits it at the caret; Backspace at the start of an item joins it to the item above (an empty item is deleted), like in Streams. - **Block menu** - Shift-Enter: insert a new paragraph, heading, list, quote or code block after the selection, or turn the selection into another type. - **Key overview** - press `?` in an outline (or its small ? button) for a table of all keys; the *keys* tab shows the same. Every key is configurable in the settings tab with TW's shortcut editor. - **Transclusions** - a marker on `{{...}}` lines; Enter opens the target in outline mode. - **Safe writes** - every write is a splice of a known range; changed text is relocated or refused, never guessed. ## Prerequisites - TiddlyWiki 5.4.0 or later (JS modules: server restart or reload needed after install) - Optional: `rimir/theme`, `rimir/doc-template` ## Quick Start 1. Install the plugin and restart the server. 2. Open a wikitext tiddler and press *outline* in its view toolbar. 3. Click a block; Up/Down select, Alt-Down moves, Tab indents. 4. Enter edits, Ctrl-Enter saves. 5. `?` shows all keys. Wikitext only; Markdown is not supported yet. llm-inline `AI:` lines do not fire from outline edits. Approach The tiddler is rendered unchanged. A JS widget, `$outline`, wraps the normal body transclusion, walks the rendered widget tree and stamps `data-ol-*` attributes on the DOM node of each unit. One delegated `keydown` and `click` handler lives on the widget's container. Operations are splices of known text ranges. Wrapper elements inside the body are avoided on purpose: they would change the HTML and break CSS such as `ul > li`. The one exception is the widget's own container: while outline mode is on, the whole body sits inside `div.rr-ol-frame > div.rr-ol` (the frame also holds the key overview), so selectors such as `.tc-tiddler-body > p` no longer match (use `.tc-tiddler-body p` or also match `.tc-tiddler-body > .rr-ol-frame > .rr-ol > p`). !! Parts |!File |!Role | |`model.js` |Collects units from the widget tree: start, end, kind, level, parent, siblings | |`text-utils.js`, `dom-utils.js` |Pure text helpers; DOM lookup shared by widget and editor | |`formats.js` |Registry of format adapters | |`format-wikitext.js` |Wikitext adapter: indent, promote, move, replace, insertNew, remove, deleteUnit, merge, editSource, isMultiline | |`outline-widget.js` |The `$outline` widget: unit-to-DOM mapping, stamps, selection, writes | |`outline-keys.js` |Key dispatch through `$:/config/shortcuts/outline-*`; toggles the key overview | |`keys/*`, `ui/keys-table`, `keys.tid` |Key groups (caption, hint, list of shortcut names), the overview table, the keys tab | |`outline-editor.js` |In-place editor: temp tiddler, placeholder, save, continue, conflict handling | |`outline-menu.js` |Menus at the selection: block menu (Shift-Enter: insert / convert / edit) and delete confirmation (Delete); keyboard and mouse | |`language/blocks.multids` |Labels of the block types and menu groups | |`ui/*` |Toolbar button and icon, body template and its filter, help bar (? button and overview), editor template, transclusion marker | |`styles.tid` |Selection frame and item box, compact editor, marker | !! Routing `ui/toolbar-button` toggles `$:/state/rimir/outline/on/` (`yes`/`no`). `ui/body-filter` (a `$:/tags/ViewTemplateBodyFilter` entry) routes eligible tiddlers with state `yes` to `ui/body`, which renders `<$outline>` around the usual block transclusion, plus the ? button and, while `$:/temp/rimir/outline/help/<title>` is `yes`, the key overview. Both sit outside `<$outline>`, so they never become units; the widget only sets and deletes that temp tiddler (`?`, Escape). !! Editor The editor is a real TW edit widget bound to a temp tiddler (`$:/temp/rimir/outline/...`), placed where the unit was. It lives outside the rendered body's widget tree, so a re-render of the body does not destroy it. Typing changes only the temp tiddler; the real tiddler changes once per save. The buffer holds the unit's content only: an item's marker and a heading's `!`s (plus the spaces after them) stay in the tiddler and are not part of the edit (`editSource`/`replace` in the adapter). `ui/editor` renders a compact textarea (no toolbar, SimpleEngine) or, with `$:/config/rimir/outline/full-editor` = `yes`, the full text editor with toolbar. !! Block menu Shift-Enter in selection mode opens `.rr-ol-menu`, absolutely positioned below the selected unit in `.rr-ol`. Its entries: //Insert after// (every block type; not for a single list item) and //Turn into// (the adapter's `convertTypes`). Insert opens a new-unit editor with a `blockType` (kept in the buffer field `outline-block-type`); saving calls the adapter's `insertBlock`, which puts a new heading after the anchor heading's whole section and any other block right after the heading line (`insertsAfterSubtree`; the editor is placed accordingly). Turn into runs `operate("convert", type)`: a bullet switches its marker character with all its siblings of that level (and their sub-items at that marker position), a whole list at all levels; paragraphs, headings and code blocks are rewritten from their content and set apart by blank lines. `convert` parses its result again and refuses it unless the new unit is where the old one was and the unit count changed only by an added list unit. !! Selection frame Units get the class `rr-ol-selected`. A list item's element contains its sub-items, so for an item with sub-items the frame is an overlay box (`.rr-ol-selbox`, absolutely positioned in `.rr-ol`) around the item's own lines, measured with a DOM range up to the nested list. It is redrawn on every selection change and when the outline container resizes (ResizeObserver). A re-render of an ancestor (for example a changed `$:/tags/Global` or `$:/tags/Macro` tiddler re-renders the page template) or closing the tiddler destroys the `$outline` widget. A buffer that differs from what the editor started with is then kept: it carries `outline-orig-source`, `outline-orig-start`, `outline-orig-text`, `outline-is-new` and `outline-unit-kind`, and the next `$outline` widget of the tiddler reopens the editor at the unit, located as on save (or with the conflict notice when the unit is gone). Escape and switching outline mode off discard it. !! Writes A single `wiki.addTiddler` of the old tiddler plus the new `text` and modification fields. Before writing, the text must equal the text the positions were computed from, otherwise the view re-renders first. If the text is this view's own last write (a key pressed before the refresh after a write), the operation goes on on the rebuilt mapping; after any other change nothing is written. Structural operations pass a model guard (`checkOp` in `model.js`) before they are written: the result is parsed again, and a move must keep the unit count and the kinds and levels; indent/promote must keep the unit count and change only the operated subtree's levels, by exactly one. Anything else is refused without a write. Which tiddlers can be outlined? Wikitext tiddlers (`text/vnd.tiddlywiki`) that are not drafts, system tiddlers, `code-body` or `hide-body` tiddlers. v1 is wikitext only; Markdown comes later through a second format adapter. !! Where does the button show? In the view toolbar, per tiddler. State is `$:/state/rimir/outline/on/<title>`. !! Can I move a unit into another list or section? Not yet. Moves stay inside the parent: at the first or last child, Alt-Up/Down do nothing. Moving across parents is a planned follow-up. !! Are widgets and macros editable inside? No. `<$list>`, `<$reveal>`, macro and procedure calls are single units: select, move or edit their source as a whole. Only plain HTML containers are opened. !! Plugins that replace core widgets (copy buttons on code blocks, ...)? A plugin can replace a core widget with its own `\widget` definition, for example `$codeblock` (kookma's utility plugin adds a caption and a copy button). The replacement renders without source positions; outline assigns it to the next unit of that type in document order, and frames, edits and moves it like any other block. What it renders inside stays untouched. !! Why can't I select a block? Units that render nothing (for example a procedure call with empty output) have no DOM node and cannot be selected. !! What happens when I save an empty unit? A unit without children is deleted. A unit with children is not: the save is refused with a notice. A new unit (from Enter) that stays empty writes nothing. !! What if the tiddler changes while I edit? Your text is kept. On save the unit is looked up again by its original source: if it occurs exactly once, the save goes there; otherwise the editor stays open with a notice. !! Two views of the same tiddler? Only one view can edit at a time. !! What happens to an unsaved edit? Escape or toggling outline mode off discards it. If you changed the text and the view is rendered again (for example after a global macro changed) or you close the tiddler, the text is kept: the editor opens again at the unit as soon as the tiddler is shown in outline mode. If the unit is gone by then, the editor opens with the "changed underneath" notice, so you can copy your text. Kept text lives in a `$:/temp/` tiddler and is gone after a reload. !! Why does Alt-Up/Down add a blank line? When a list, code block or table is followed directly (single line break) by a paragraph, swapping them as they are would merge the paragraph with its new neighbour. Such blocks get a blank line between them. Items and headings keep their line breaks. A comment (or other text that is not a unit) between the two blocks is kept and set apart by blank lines too. !! Why does Alt-Up/Down sometimes do nothing? A move only swaps a unit with its neighbour inside the same parent, and only with a neighbour of the same class (heading with heading of the same level, item with item of the same level, other blocks with other blocks). Before writing, outline re-parses the result; if the swap would change the units (for example a heading section whose last paragraph would merge with the next block), the move is refused and the text stays unchanged. Add a blank line between the blocks by hand and try again. !! Do Tab and Alt-Up/Down work while I edit? Yes. They save your text, indent, promote or move the unit with its subtree, and keep editing it at its new place with the cursor where it was. With empty text they do nothing. !! My CSS for `.tc-tiddler-body > p` stopped working While outline mode is on, the body is wrapped in `div.rr-ol`, so child selectors of `.tc-tiddler-body` no longer match. Use a descendant selector (`.tc-tiddler-body p`) or also match `.tc-tiddler-body > .rr-ol > p`. !! Do `AI:` lines of llm-inline fire? No. Outline writes bypass `th-saving-tiddler`, which llm-inline listens to. `AI:` lines typed in outline mode do not fire; they do after a normal editor save. !! Why doesn't the editor show the `*` or `!`? The editor edits a unit's content. The list marker and the heading level are structure: change them with Tab/Shift-Tab. If you type the item's own marker at the start anyway (for example `* ` in a `*` item), it is dropped instead of doubled. !! How do I put a line break into a bullet? Shift-Enter in the editor. In wikitext a list item (and a heading) is one source line, and a real line break would end it: the next line would become a paragraph that swallows the following items. So line breaks in items and headings are saved as `<br>`, and an existing `<br>` shows as a line break when you edit. Enter stays //save and new item//. Paragraphs and other blocks keep real line breaks. !! Why does switching one bullet to numbered switch its neighbours too? In wikitext the list type is the marker character, and items of one level with different characters do not form one list: one numbered item among bullets would cut the list into three. So //Turn into// switches all items of that level under the same parent; their sub-items keep their own type. !! Do editor plugins work? Yes, the editor is TW's own edit widget. AutoComplete handles Enter, Escape, Tab and the arrows first; outline keys act only if the event was not consumed. !! Does Tab leave the page? No, while a unit is selected Tab is used for indent. </$fill> </$transclude> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/overview":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/overview","created":"20261120120000000","modified":"20261120120000000","rdt.hub-category":"tools","rdt.hub-category-name":"Tools","rdt.hub-order":"6","rdt.plugin-key":"outline","rdt.plugin-name":"outline","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Select, edit, move and indent blocks of a tiddler in place","rdt.order":"1","rdt.section":"Overview","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! What it does Outline mode brings the Streams workflow to a normal tiddler. Switch it on for a tiddler with the //outline// button in the view toolbar. The tiddler renders as before; every block that comes from its own text becomes selectable. Select a block, edit it in place, move it, indent it. Each action rewrites the right part of that one tiddler's text. !! How you use it # Press //outline// in the view toolbar (the button is shown for wikitext tiddlers only, not for drafts, system tiddlers, `code-body` or `hide-body` tiddlers). # Click a block or press Up/Down (Left/Right: parent / first child). A whole list counts as one block for Up/Down; Right enters it, Ctrl-Up/Down step through every item. A blue frame marks the selected unit. A small badge in the right margin names each unit's type (paragraph, h2, code-block, bullet, ...), so heading levels and block types are easy to tell apart; the editor field carries the badge of what it edits. The settings switch it to headings only or off. On a list item it frames only the item's own line; moves still take its sub-items along. # Alt-Up/Alt-Down move it, Tab/Shift-Tab indent or promote it. Its subtree goes along. # Enter (or a double-click) opens the editor in place, the caret at the end of the text: a compact one-line field (the full editor with toolbar is a setting). It shows the content only, without the list marker or heading `!`s, so editing never changes the nesting. Ctrl-Enter saves, Enter saves and opens a new unit, Escape discards. Ctrl-Up/Down save and move the editor to the previous/next unit. # Delete removes the selected unit with everything below it, after a yes/no menu; on a heading the menu also offers to delete just the heading line. In the editor, Enter in the middle of a list item splits it at the caret, and Backspace at its start merges it into the item above. # Shift-Enter opens the block menu: insert a new block of a type after the selection, or turn the selection into another type. # On a transclusion line, Enter opens the target tiddler, already in outline mode. # `?` (or the small ? button at the top right) shows all keys next to the outline; Escape closes it. The //keys// tab has the same overview, the settings tab changes the keys. !! Units * List items (`*`, `#`, `;`, `:`, `>`) - the item's own lines; nested items are its subtree. * Lists as a whole. * Headings, with their section (up to the next heading of the same or a higher level) as subtree. * Paragraphs, code blocks, tables. * Plain HTML containers (`<div>`, `<section>`, ...) are opened: their inner blocks are units, and the container is one too. * Transclusion lines (`{{...}}`, `<$transclude/>`). * Widgets (`<$list>`, `<$reveal>`, ...) and macro or procedure calls: opaque, one unit each. Pragmas (`\define`, `\procedure`, `\import`, ...) are never units. A unit that renders nothing cannot be selected. !! Read-only wikis With `$:/status/IsReadOnly` = yes, only navigation (selection, transclusion jump) works. </$fill> </$transclude> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/reference":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/reference","created":"20261120120000000","modified":"20261120120000000","rdt.hub-category":"tools","rdt.hub-category-name":"Tools","rdt.hub-order":"6","rdt.plugin-key":"outline","rdt.plugin-name":"outline","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Select, edit, move and indent blocks of a tiddler in place","rdt.order":"6","rdt.section":"Reference","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! Keys |!Shortcut tiddler |!Default |!Action | |`outline-up` / `outline-down` |Up / Down |Select previous / next unit. A whole list counts as one block: Down from a selected list goes to the block after it, Up from below a list selects the whole list; inside a list they go item by item | |`outline-up-deep` / `outline-down-deep` |ctrl-Up / ctrl-Down |Select previous / next unit in document order, also into lists (from below a list: its last item) | |`outline-parent` / `outline-child` |Left / Right |Select the parent unit (item of a sub-item, whole list of a top-level item, heading of a section) / the first child | |`outline-move-up` / `outline-move-down` |alt-Up / alt-Down |Swap with previous / next sibling | |`outline-indent` / `outline-promote` |Tab / shift-Tab |Demote / promote by one level | |`outline-edit` |Enter |Edit in place (on a transclusion Enter opens the target) | |`outline-delete` |Delete |Delete the unit with its subtree, after a confirmation menu (see Delete) | |`outline-menu` |shift-Enter |Block menu: insert a new block after the unit, or turn it into another type; Up/Down, Enter runs, Escape closes | |`outline-open` |Enter |Open the transclusion target in outline mode | |`outline-clear` |Escape |Clear selection | |`outline-save` |ctrl-Enter |Save the edit | |`outline-continue` |Enter |Save and open a new unit (single-line units). In the middle of a list item's text: split it (see Split) | |`outline-newline` |shift-Enter |Newline in the editor (saved as `<br>` in list items and headings) | |`outline-indent` / `outline-promote` |Tab / shift-Tab |In the editor too: save, indent / promote, keep editing | |`outline-move-up` / `outline-move-down` |alt-Up / alt-Down |In the editor too: save, move, keep editing | |`outline-edit-up` |ctrl-Up |Editor only: save and edit the previous unit | |`outline-edit-down` |ctrl-Down |Editor only: save and edit the next unit | |`outline-merge` |Backspace |Editor, caret at the start of a list item: merge it into the item above (see Merge) | |`outline-cancel` |Escape |Discard the edit | |`outline-help` |shift-slash |Show / hide the key overview. `?` always works too, whatever the keyboard layout; Escape closes it | All are `$:/config/shortcuts/<name>`; descriptions are in `$:/config/ShortcutInfo/<name>`. Change them in the settings tab (the core shortcut editor, press the key to record it, platform variants included) or in ControlPanel > Keyboard Shortcuts. !! Type badges |!`data-ol-type` |!Unit | |`paragraph`, `code-block`, `table`, `quote`, `rule` |Blocks (`p`, `pre`, `table`, `blockquote`, `hr`; other blocks: their tag name) | |`h1` … `h6` |Headings | |`bullet`, `numbered`, `term`, `definition`, `quote` |List items (by their list: `ul`, `ol`, `dt`/`dd`, `blockquote`) | |`bullet-list`, `numbered-list`, `definitions`, `quote` |Whole lists (badge in the left margin) | |`transclusion`, `widget` |Transclusion lines, widgets and macro calls | |tag name (`div`, ...) |Opened HTML containers (badge in the left margin) | The widget sets `data-ol-type` on each unit's first DOM node (`unitType` in `dom-utils.js`); CSS shows it as `::after`, absolutely positioned, so the layout does not change. The editor field gets the type of the unit it edits, of the chosen block type, or of its anchor (a new item); an item edited inside its `li` keeps the `li`'s badge. !! Key overview The //keys// tab and the overlay (`?` in an outline, or the small ? button at its top right) show the same table, `$:/plugins/rimir/outline/ui/keys-table`, with the keys read live from the config. Its groups are the tiddlers listed in `$:/plugins/rimir/outline/key-groups`: each has a `caption`, an optional `hint`, a `list` of shortcut names and, optionally, text shown after the keys (the fixed block menu keys). The settings tab uses the same groups. A double-click on a unit opens the editor on it (on a transclusion: its line; links and buttons keep their click). In multi-line units (code blocks, tables, widgets, `"""` items) Enter is a plain newline and only Ctrl-Enter saves. !! Indent and promote * Lists: a list item and its subtree lines get one more of the item's last marker character (`#b` becomes `##b`, `*b` `**b`, `#*` `#**`). No previous sibling: no-op. Promote removes one marker character; depth 1 is a no-op. * Headings: one `!` more on the heading and every heading in its section; no-op if one would pass 6. Promote removes one; level 1 is a no-op. * Other units: Tab and Shift-Tab do nothing. !! Move Swap the unit's whole subtree with the adjacent sibling's whole subtree, blank-line separators preserved. Blocks other than items and headings that touch (a single line break) get a blank line between them and before the following content, so a paragraph cannot absorb its neighbour. First/last child: no-op. * List item: siblings are items of the same list at the same depth. * Heading: siblings are headings of the same level in the same parent. * Other blocks: siblings are blocks in the same section (or HTML container, or root) before any sub-heading. !! Delete The unit goes with its subtree: an item with its sub-items, a heading with its section, a list with its items, a container with its contents. An only item takes its list along and an only child its container (neither can stay empty). Separators as for a blank save: one blank line stays between the neighbours. The selection goes to the unit that now starts there. |!Selected |!Menu | |Heading with a section |Yes, the heading and its section (N blocks) · Just the heading (its section joins the one above) · Cancel | |Whole list / item with sub-items / container |Yes, ... (N items / sub-items / blocks) · Cancel | |Anything else |Yes, delete · Cancel | The first entry is active: Delete, Enter deletes; Escape cancels. List items without sub-items are deleted at once while `$:/config/rimir/outline/quick-delete-items` is `yes` (the default); `no` asks for them too. The model guard refuses a result that removes other units than these (e.g. two lists that would merge). !! Merge (Backspace) In the editor, caret at the very start of a list item (nothing selected): the item's text goes to the end of the item above it in the list (the previous item in document order: the parent, or the last sub-item of the previous sibling), the item's line goes, its sub-items keep their lines and levels. The editor continues in the item above, at the join. An empty item is simply deleted (also one with sub-items) and the editor goes to the end of the item above; an empty new item is discarded the same way. The first item of a list, other units and multi-line items: a normal Backspace. !! Split (Enter) In the editor, caret inside a list item's text (not at its start or end, nothing selected): the text before the caret stays in the item, the text after it goes to a new item directly below, which is edited with the caret at its start. The new item is a sibling with the same marker; when the item has sub-items it becomes their first one, so the sub-items stay with the item. Backspace at the new item's start (merge) gives back the original line. !! New unit (Enter) * List item: same marker, after the item's whole subtree. * Heading: paragraph directly under the heading line. * Paragraph: paragraph after it. !! Block menu |!Selected |!Insert after |!Turn into | |Paragraph |Paragraph, Heading 1–3, Bulleted/Numbered list, Quote, Code block |Heading 1–3, Bulleted/Numbered list, Quote, Code block | |Heading |the same (a heading goes after the section, other blocks right below the heading) |Paragraph, Bulleted/Numbered list, Quote, Code block | |Code block |the same |Paragraph, Bulleted/Numbered list, Quote | |Whole list |the same |Bulleted ↔ Numbered (all levels) | |List item |– |Bulleted ↔ Numbered (with all its siblings of that level) | |Transclusion |the same, plus //Edit this line// first |– | !! State and config |!Tiddler |!Purpose | |`$:/state/rimir/outline/on/<title>` |Outline mode on (`yes`) / off | |`$:/temp/rimir/outline/...` |Editor buffer, selection and open key overview (`help/<title>`) while active | |`$:/config/rimir/outline/badges` |Type badges: `all` (default), `headings` (h1–h6 only) or `off`. Sets class `rr-ol-badges-<mode>` on the frame; the badge text is the unit's `data-ol-type` | |`$:/config/rimir/outline/quick-delete-items` |`yes` (default): Delete removes list items without sub-items without asking; `no`: always ask | |`$:/config/rimir/outline/full-editor` |`yes`: full text editor with toolbar; otherwise (default `no`) the compact one-line editor | </$fill> </$transclude> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/tw-internals":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/tw-internals","created":"20261120120000000","modified":"20261120120000000","rdt.hub-category":"tools","rdt.hub-category-name":"Tools","rdt.hub-order":"6","rdt.plugin-key":"outline","rdt.plugin-name":"outline","rdt.plugin-subtitle":"Select, edit, move and indent blocks of a tiddler in place","rdt.order":"7","rdt.section":"TW Internals","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$transclude $tiddler="$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/templates/page"> <$fill $name="body"> !! Parser positions The plugin relies on the wikitext parser's source offsets. `WikiParser.parseBlock` sets `start`, `end` and `rule` on every top-level block node. The list rule sets them on each list item: from the marker to the end of the item's own line, nested child lines excluded. Every widget keeps its parse node as `widget.parseTreeNode`, so a widget tree walk recovers the ranges. Units are recomputed after every render and are valid only for the text they were computed from. !! `{{X}}` is a "tiddler" node A block transclusion `{{X}}` parses to a node of type `tiddler`, not `transclude`; the walker maps it to the transclusion unit. Widgets rendered from a transcluded tiddler carry offsets into //that// tiddler's text, so descent stops at a transclude to another tiddler. !! Widget mapping rule A unit's DOM node is found by matching the parse node's `start` and tag; `end` is the tie-breaker when several widgets share a start (for example a list and its first item). !! Pragmas and typed blocks A pragma such as `\define` parses to a `set` node that wraps the rest of the tree; the walker steps through it, and the pragma itself is never a unit. For `$$$` typed blocks the parser starts the node at the line after the `$$$` header, so the widget match uses that line as the unit's anchor instead of the unit start (see `outline-widget.js`). !! Pin tests `test/test-parser-pins.js` pins the offsets for list items, a heading and a paragraph, a block transclusion (`{{X}}` parses to a `tiddler` node), pragma wrapping (`\define` yields a `set` node that wraps the following blocks), a code block, a table and a block-mode HTML container. Widgets are not pinned. A TW update that changes them fails the suite loudly. !! Why writes bypass `th-saving-tiddler` A write is `wiki.addTiddler` of the old tiddler with new `text` plus `getModificationFields()`. It is not an editor save, and a single splice per action must not trigger editor-save hooks. Consequence: listeners on `th-saving-tiddler`, such as llm-inline's `AI:` lines, do not fire. !! Editor and AutoComplete AutoComplete listens on `document` in the capture phase, so its handler runs before the outline key handler, which checks `event.defaultPrevented`. </$fill> </$transclude> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/documentation":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/documentation","type":"text/vnd.tiddlywiki","text":"<$list filter="[[$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template]plugin-type[plugin]]" variable="ignore"> {{$:/plugins/rimir/outline/doc/overview||$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template/doc-viewer}} </$list> <$list filter="[[$:/plugins/rimir/doc-template]plugin-type[plugin]!match[plugin]]" variable="ignore"> <div class="rr-settings-info-card"> ''doc-template'' plugin is not installed. See the <<tag readme>> tab for documentation. </div> </$list> "},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/dom-utils.js":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/dom-utils.js","text":"/*\ title: $:/plugins/rimir/outline/dom-utils.js type: application/javascript module-type: library DOM helpers shared by outline-keys.js and outline-editor.js. They work on the browser DOM and on TW's fake DOM (no nextSibling/contains there; removeChild keeps parentNode). \*/ "use strict"; exports.setClass = function(node, cls, on) { var list = (node.className || "").split(" ").filter(function(c) { return c && c !== cls; }); if(on) { list.push(cls); } if(list.length) { node.className = list.join(" "); } else if(node.removeAttribute) { node.removeAttribute("class"); } }; exports.focus = function(node) { if(node && node.focus) { node.focus({preventScroll: true}); } }; exports.scrollIntoView = function(node) { if(node && node.scrollIntoView) { node.scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"}); } }; // True for input/textarea/select and contenteditable elements and their descendants exports.isEditable = function(node) { for(; node && node.nodeType === 1; node = node.parentNode) { var tag = (node.tagName || "").toLowerCase(); if(tag === "input" || tag === "textarea" || tag === "select" || node.isContentEditable) { return true; } } return false; }; exports.nextSiblingOf = function(node) { if(node.nextSibling !== undefined) { return node.nextSibling; } var siblings = node.parentNode ? node.parentNode.childNodes : [], i = siblings.indexOf(node); return i === -1 ? null : (siblings[i + 1] || null); }; exports.firstChildOf = function(node) { return node.firstChild || null; }; // True when `node` is attached below (or is) `ancestor` exports.isInside = function(node, ancestor) { if(!node || !ancestor) { return false; } if(ancestor.contains) { return ancestor.contains(node); } while(node && node !== ancestor) { var parent = node.parentNode; if(!parent || parent.childNodes.indexOf(node) === -1) { return false; } node = parent; } return node === ancestor; }; function tagOf(node) { return node ? String(node.tagName || node.tag || "").toLowerCase() : ""; } var LIST_TYPES = {ul: "bullet-list", ol: "numbered-list", dl: "definitions", blockquote: "quote"}, ITEM_TYPES = {ul: "bullet", ol: "numbered", blockquote: "quote"}, BLOCK_TYPES = {p: "paragraph", pre: "code-block", table: "table", blockquote: "quote", hr: "rule"}, // Types of the block menu (format-wikitext BLOCK_TYPES) as badge types NEW_BLOCK_TYPES = {paragraph: "paragraph", heading1: "h1", heading2: "h2", heading3: "h3", bulleted: "bullet", numbered: "numbered", quote: "quote", code: "code-block"}; /* Badge type of a unit (kind) from its first DOM node: paragraph, h1-h6, code-block, table, quote, rule, bullet, numbered, term, definition, bullet-list, numbered-list, definitions, transclusion, widget, or the tag name. Shown by CSS (attr(data-ol-type)) when badges are on. */ exports.unitType = function(kind, node) { var tag = tagOf(node); switch(kind) { case "heading": return /^h[1-6]$/.test(tag) ? tag : "heading"; case "item": return tag === "dt" ? "term" : tag === "dd" ? "definition" : ITEM_TYPES[tagOf(node.parentNode)] || "item"; case "list": return LIST_TYPES[tag] || "list"; case "block": return BLOCK_TYPES[tag] || tag || "block"; case "transclusion": return "transclusion"; case "widget": return "widget"; default: return tag || kind; } }; exports.newBlockType = function(blockType) { return NEW_BLOCK_TYPES[blockType] || ""; }; ","type":"application/javascript","module-type":"library"},"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/format-wikitext.js":{"title":"$:/plugins/rimir/outline/format-wikitext.js","text":"/*\ title: $:/plugins/rimir/outline/format-wikitext.js type: application/javascript module-type: outline-format Wikitext adapter: indent, promote, move, replace, insertNew, remove, deleteUnit, merge, split. Functions take (text, model, id) and return null or {text, select}. \*/ "use strict"; var utils = require("$:/plugins/rimir/outline/text-utils.js"), outlineModel = require("$:/plugins/rimir/outline/model.js"); exports.types = ["text/vnd.tiddlywiki", ""]; // A separator that contains an empty line var BLANK_LINE = /\n[ \t]*\r?\n/; // Units of `kind` whose start lies in the subtree of u (u included) function subtreeUnits(model, u, kind) { return model.units.filter(function(d) { return d.kind === kind && d.start >= u.start && d.start < u.subtreeEnd; }); } // positions: [{pos, insert}] / removals; applied from the end backwards function apply(text, edits) { edits.sort(function(a, b) { return b.pos - a.pos; }); edits.forEach(function(e) { text = utils.splice(text, e.pos, e.pos + e.remove, e.insert); }); return text; } function selectFor(u, edits) { // units start never moves: edits at u.start insert before it only for headings, where start stays return u.start; } exports.indent = function(text, model, id) { var u = model.units[id], edits; if(!u) { return null; } if(u.kind === "item") { var sibs = u.parent === -1 ? model.roots : model.units[u.parent].children, i = sibs.indexOf(id); if(i < 1 || model.units[sibs[i - 1]].kind !== "item") { return null; } var c = u.marker.charAt(u.level - 1); edits = subtreeUnits(model, u, "item").map(function(d) { return {pos: d.start + u.level, remove: 0, insert: c}; }); } else if(u.kind === "heading") { var hs = subtreeUnits(model, u, "heading"); if(hs.some(function(h) { return h.level >= 6; })) { return null; } edits = hs.map(function(h) { return {pos: h.start, remove: 0, insert: "!"}; }); } else { return null; } return {text: apply(text, edits), select: selectFor(u, edits)}; }; exports.promote = function(text, model, id) { var u = model.units[id], edits; if(!u) { return null; } if(u.kind === "item") { if(u.level <= 1) { return null; } edits = subtreeUnits(model, u, "item").map(function(d) { return {pos: d.start + u.level - 1, remove: 1, insert: ""}; }); } else if(u.kind === "heading") { if(u.level <= 1) { return null; } edits = subtreeUnits(model, u, "heading").map(function(h) { return {pos: h.start, remove: 1, insert: ""}; }); } else { return null; } return {text: apply(text, edits), select: selectFor(u, edits)}; }; /* Swap the unit's whole subtree with the adjacent sibling of the same class (heading vs non-heading). Items and headings keep the separators as they are. Other blocks that touch (single line break) get a blank line between them and before the content after the pair, because after the swap a paragraph would otherwise absorb the block after it. Non-whitespace between the blocks (a comment) is kept and set apart by blank lines. */ exports.move = function(text, model, id, dir) { var u = model.units[id]; if(!u || (dir !== -1 && dir !== 1)) { return null; } var sibs = u.parent === -1 ? model.roots : model.units[u.parent].children, i = sibs.indexOf(id), n = sibs[i + dir]; if(i < 0 || n === undefined) { return null; } var o = model.units[n]; if((o.kind === "heading") !== (u.kind === "heading")) { return null; } if((u.kind === "heading" || u.kind === "item") && (o.kind !== u.kind || o.level !== u.level)) { return null; } var a = dir < 0 ? o : u, b = dir < 0 ? u : o, A = text.substring(a.start, a.subtreeEnd), sep = text.substring(a.subtreeEnd, b.start), B = text.substring(b.start, b.subtreeEnd), rest = text.substring(b.subtreeEnd); if(u.kind !== "item" && u.kind !== "heading") { var nl = utils.eol(text), gap = /^(?:[ \t]*\r?\n)*/.exec(rest)[0]; if(/\S/.test(sep)) { // Keep anything between the blocks (e.g. a comment), set apart by blank lines on both sides sep = nl + nl + sep.trim() + nl + nl; } else if(!BLANK_LINE.test(sep)) { sep = nl + nl; } // Only whole line breaks are normalised, so the next line keeps its indentation if(/\S/.test(rest) && !BLANK_LINE.test(gap)) { rest = nl + nl + rest.substring(gap.length); } } return { text: text.substring(0, a.start) + B + sep + A + rest, select: dir < 0 ? a.start : a.start + B.length + sep.length }; }; // Replace the unit's own source with newSource /* Offset where the unit's content starts: after an item's marker or a heading's "!"s and the spaces after them. Outline mode only adds data attributes, a selection frame and key handling. * ''Units'' — list items, lists, headings (with their sections), paragraphs, code blocks, tables, opened HTML containers, transclusion lines, and widgets or macro calls (one opaque unit each). * ''Type badges'' — a small, faint label next to every unit shows what it is (paragraph, h2, code-block, bullet, ...), also on the editor field; they take no space. Settings: all (default), headings only, off. * ''Selection'' — click, Up/Down in document order, Left/Right to the parent / first child, Escape clears. * ''Move'' — Alt-Up/Alt-Down swap a unit with its sibling, carrying its subtree. Moves stay inside the parent. * ''Indent'' — Tab/Shift-Tab demote/promote list items (one marker character) and headings (one `!`) with their subtrees. * ''In-place editor'' — Enter or a double-click opens TW's own edit widget at the unit (AutoComplete and other editor plugins work): a compact one-line field by default, optionally the full editor with toolbar. Lists and headings are edited without their marker; nesting stays with Tab/Shift-Tab. Ctrl-Enter saves, Enter saves and starts a new unit, Escape discards, Ctrl-Up/Down save and move the editor to the previous/next unit. * ''Delete'' — the Delete key removes the selection with everything below it, after a small yes/no menu (a heading: with its section or just the heading); list items without sub-items go at once (a setting). * ''Split and merge'' — Enter in the middle of a list item splits it at the caret; Backspace at the start of an item joins it to the item above (an empty item is deleted), like in Streams. * ''Block menu'' — Shift-Enter: insert a new paragraph, heading, list, quote or code block after the selection, or turn the selection into another type (a bullet list into a numbered one, a paragraph into a heading, ...). * ''Key overview'' — press `?` in an outline (or its small ? button) for a table of all keys; the //keys// tab shows the same. Every key is configurable in the settings tab with TW's shortcut editor. * ''Transclusions'' — a small marker on `{{…}}` lines; Enter opens the target in outline mode. * ''Safe writes'' — every write is a splice of a known range; if the text changed underneath, the edit is relocated or refused, never guessed. !! Prerequisites * TiddlyWiki 5.4.0 or later (JS modules: server restart or reload needed after install) * Optional: `rimir/theme` (`rr-` styles in settings), `rimir/doc-template` (branded docs) !!
